subject.title: gateway HTTP ingress skips browser Origin check under auth.mode none (cross-origin CSRF on state-changing routes)

question: Should Gateway HTTP reject requests carrying a disallowed browser `Origin` before accepting `gateway.auth.mode="none"`, while preserving origin-less private-ingress clients?
rationale: The issue is source-backed, but the fix changes the security and compatibility contract for an explicit no-auth mode documented for private ingress.

options.title: Enforce Origin for browser HTTP
options.body: Reject any HTTP request with a disallowed `Origin` before the none-mode success return, matching the WebSocket invariant while preserving origin-less clients.

options.title: Document none as no CSRF boundary
options.body: Leave the current behavior intact and update docs/audit language to say no-auth HTTP routes do not enforce browser Origin checks.

options.title: Add opt-in strict policy
options.body: Preserve current none-mode behavior by default and add a strict Origin policy knob, accepting the new config and upgrade complexity.

recommendation.title: Enforce Origin for browser HTTP
recommendation.body: Reject any HTTP request with a disallowed `Origin` before the none-mode success return, matching the WebSocket invariant while preserving origin-less clients.
